{
  "root_cause": "The focus trap's tryFocus function does not handle exceptions when calling node.focus(), which can occur if the node becomes detached or hidden during the focus attempt. When the #more button's click handler runs unexpectedly (as observed in the DOM state after step 2), it removes itself and updates the list. During the subsequent Tab press from #close, the focus trap attempts to refocus #close (the only remaining tabbable node), but if this focus call throws an exception (e.g., due to a race condition with DOM mutations), the focus is lost and defaults to the body, breaking the trap.",
  "repair_strategy": "Wrap the node.focus() call in tryFocus with a try-catch block. On exception, recursively attempt to focus the initial focus node (via getInitialFocusNode()) as a fallback. This ensures that if focusing the intended node fails due to transient DOM issues, the trap recovers by focusing a known focusable node instead of allowing focus to escape to the body.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Keyboard focus will remain trapped within the dialog even if transient DOM mutations cause occasional focus failures on individual elements, preserving modal keyboard navigation compliance.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Potential infinite recursion if both the target node and initial focus node fail to focus (mitigated by the recursion being limited to two attempts in practice).",
    "Slight performance overhead from try-catch during focus attempts.",
    "If the initial focus node is also unfocusable, focus may still be lost (but this is no worse than the current behavior)."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that pressing Tab from #close keeps focus within the dialog after the #more button has been removed.",
    "Verify that the Escape key still closes the dialog and returns focus to the #open button.",
    "Verify that initial focus still lands on #close when the dialog opens.",
    "Verify that focusing a node that throws an exception (e.g., detached node) falls back to the initial focus node without crashing."
  ]
}
